html:
The Tsnungwe are a Native American people of the lower South Fork of the Trinity River in northwestern California, around Burnt Ranch, Salyer and Willow Creek. Their name means "people of Ironside Mountain".

They speak a dialect of Hupa, an Athabaskan language, and are close relatives of the Hupa people downriver. They lived from salmon, acorns and game. The Gold Rush brought miners to the Trinity River in the 1850s, and with them violence and disease. Their neighbours included the Chimariko and the New River Shasta.
